R12 (low, process): writing prose or scripts through a shell heredoc corrupts them in this environment. Write scripts and messages to files with file_editor and execute the file. It recurred this run and aborted a STATE.md update before it wrote anything.

R13 (low): PlannedStep.capability is derived from the tool catalog, so a plan cannot understate its authority. Any future plan construction path must go through PlannedStep or it reintroduces the gap; the derived field is what enforces it, not the use case.

R14 (new, low): the tool-invocation trail stores only arguments_digest, so an auditor can prove a call happened but cannot reconstruct its payload. That is deliberate (the trail must not become a second copy of note content), but a future investigation may want an explicit, separately-authorized payload-retrieval path rather than widening this one.

R15 (new, low): the audit chain seals each invocation over its predecessor, but the chain head is not anchored outside the database. An attacker who can rewrite the whole table can produce a self-consistent chain. Anchoring the head hash externally is the next hardening step, not a regression.
